PC: “Doctors” will get the “patient’s” story and be able to name the Chief Complaint (CC), obtain a History of Present Illness (HPI) and related Past Medical History (PMH) including social and family history.
Clarify the timeline and all symptom details.

Practice the “technical” subroutine. Use the mnemonic OLDCARTS (onset, location, duration, character, aggravating/associated factors, relieving factors, temporal factors, severity) to clarify symptom descriptions. Be careful to avoid bombarding the “patient” with question after question. Use the skills learned to this point to obtain this information in an open-ended fashion.

ICS: The “doctor” should get the STORY. Use empathy to understand the patient’s feelings, the context and the personal meaning of the problem for the patient. IMPORTANT: The “story” is more important than all the details of the technical subroutine.
At the end of the interview, the “doctor” retells the story—including facts and symptom details as well as the meaning for the “patient”—to the observer, “patient,” and coach.

This time they should focus on the beliefs, concerns, and feelings of the patient about this symptom experience. How will it influence their life? What are they really worried about? What is the implication for their family? Are there gender, age, spiritual, economic issues that could arise?
At the end of the interview, the “doctor” discusses the potential daily implications of this patient’s story to the other group members.
